description:
Please build a TRNSYS-based solar-assisted air heating system simulation model with microprocessor-based multi-mode control. This project simulates a solar heating system for a single-zone building located in Fresno, California, USA, evaluating the coordinated operation of solar energy collection, thermal storage, and auxiliary heating under intelligent multi-mode control during a winter/spring period.

Simulation parameters: The simulation runs from hour 0 to hour 3624 (approximately 151 days, covering January through May), with a time step of 5 minutes (5/60 hours). Integration and convergence tolerances are both set to 0.001, with a maximum of 30 iterations per time step.

Weather data: A TMY3-format weather data file is provided, located at "d:\TRNSYS18_03\Weather\US-TMY3\US_CA_FRESNO_YOSEMITE_INTL_AP_723890.tmy3". The weather data processor computes tilted surface radiation for one horizontal surface (slope 0 degrees), with a ground reflectance of 0.2.

The system is a solar-assisted forced-air heating system with microprocessor-based multi-mode control. It consists of 1 quadratic-efficiency flat-plate solar collector with second-order incidence angle modifiers, 1 vertical cylindrical stratified hot water storage tank (5 nodes, no internal heat exchangers), 2 constant-effectiveness heat exchangers (one for the solar loop and one for the auxiliary heating loop), 3 single-speed pumps (one for the solar collector loop, one for the solar heat exchanger load side, and one for the auxiliary heating loop), 1 single-speed fan/blower for the air distribution loop, 1 lumped-capacitance single-zone building model, 1 microprocessor controller with 3 comparators and 6 operating modes controlling 3 outputs, 3 psychrometric property calculators for air state point determination, 1 weather data processor, and 1 online plotter with output file.

Flat-plate solar collector with second-order incidence angle modifiers: 2 collectors connected in series with a total collector area of 8 m². The collector optical efficiency (intercept efficiency) is 0.80, the first-order heat loss coefficient (efficiency slope) is 13.0 kJ/(hr·m²·K), and the second-order heat loss coefficient (efficiency curvature) is 0.05 kJ/(hr·m²·K²). The incidence angle modifier uses a second-order model with a first-order coefficient of 0.2 and a second-order coefficient of 0.0. The collector was tested at a flow rate of 62.5 kg/(hr·m²). The working fluid specific heat is 4.19 kJ/(kg·K). The efficiency is based on inlet temperature (efficiency mode 1). The collector is installed horizontally (slope 0 degrees).

Vertical cylindrical stratified hot water storage tank (no internal heat exchangers): A vertical cylindrical tank with a volume of 1.515 m³ and a height of 1.25 m, divided into 5 equal temperature stratification nodes. The tank has uniform thermal loss coefficients of 3.325 kJ/(hr·m²·K) for the top, edge, and bottom surfaces. The fluid is water with a specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), a density of 1000 kg/m³, and a thermal conductivity of 2.224 kJ/(hr·m·K). The tank has two fluid ports: port 1 has its inlet at the top (height fraction 1.0) and outlet at the bottom (height fraction 0.0), used for the solar collector loop; port 2 has its inlet at the bottom (height fraction 0.0) and outlet at the top (height fraction 1.0), used for the load-side heat exchanger loop. No thermostats and no auxiliary heat inputs are configured. All 5 nodes are initialized at 20°C. The tank loss temperatures (top, edge, and bottom) are connected to the room zone temperature.

Solar loop constant-effectiveness heat exchanger: This heat exchanger transfers heat from the storage tank hot water to the air distribution loop. It has an effectiveness of 1.0 (ideal heat transfer). The source-side fluid specific heat is 4.19 kJ/(kg·K) (water from the tank), and the load-side fluid specific heat is 1.007 kJ/(kg·K) (air). The source side receives hot water from the tank port 2 outlet (top of tank), and the load side receives air from the auxiliary heat exchanger outlet (after psychrometric processing).

Auxiliary heating loop constant-effectiveness heat exchanger: This heat exchanger provides supplemental heating from an auxiliary hot water source to the air distribution loop. It has an effectiveness of 1.0 (ideal heat transfer). The source-side fluid specific heat is 4.19 kJ/(kg·K) (hot water), and the load-side fluid specific heat is 1.007 kJ/(kg·K) (air). The source side receives hot water from the auxiliary pump, and the load side receives return air from the building zone (after psychrometric processing).

Solar collector loop single-speed pump (Pump I): This pump circulates water through the solar collector loop. It has a rated flow rate of 500 kg/hr, a fluid specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), a rated power of 2684.0 kJ/hr, and a motor heat loss fraction of 0.0. The pump is controlled by the first output of the microprocessor controller (collector control signal).

Solar heat exchanger load-side single-speed pump (Pump II): This pump circulates water on the load side of the solar heat exchanger. It has a rated flow rate of 500 kg/hr, a fluid specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), a rated power of 2684.0 kJ/hr, and a motor heat loss fraction of 0.0. The pump is controlled by the second output of the microprocessor controller (tank discharge control signal).

Auxiliary heating loop single-speed pump (Pump III): This pump circulates hot water through the auxiliary heat exchanger. It has a rated flow rate of 500 kg/hr, a fluid specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), a rated power of 2684.0 kJ/hr, and a motor heat loss fraction of 0.0. The pump inlet fluid temperature is a constant 60°C (representing an ideal auxiliary heat source). The pump is controlled by the third output of the microprocessor controller (auxiliary heating control signal).

Single-speed fan/blower: This fan circulates air through the heating coil heat exchangers and delivers conditioned air to the building zone. It operates in relative humidity mode (humidity mode 2). The rated volumetric flow rate is 347 l/s, the rated power is 671.140939 kJ/hr, the motor efficiency is 0.90, and the motor heat loss fraction is 0.0. The fan inlet air conditions are determined by the psychrometric state after the solar heat exchanger.

Lumped-capacitance single-zone building model with internal gains: This simplified building model represents a single thermal zone. The building has a loss coefficient of 3 kJ/(hr·m²·K), a thermal capacitance of 5000 kJ/K, a surface area of 380 m², and a volume of 600 m³. The building air has a specific heat of 1.007 kJ/(kg·K) and a density of 1.2 kg/m³. The initial zone temperature is 15°C with an initial humidity ratio of 0.005. The latent heat of vaporization is 2260 kJ/kg. The building receives conditioned air from the fan and is exposed to ambient conditions from the weather data. No internal gains from lights, equipment, people, or infiltration are considered.

Microprocessor controller with 3 comparators and 6 operating modes: This is the central intelligence of the system, combining 3 differential comparators with a truth-table logic array to determine 6 possible operating modes and 3 control outputs. The comparators and their deadbands are configured as follows:
- Comparator 1 compares the solar collector outlet temperature (high input) with the storage tank bottom node temperature (low input). Turn-on deadband: 5°C, turn-off deadband: 1°C. This comparator determines whether the collector is producing useful heat relative to the tank.
- Comparator 2 compares the storage tank top node temperature (high input) with the room setpoint temperature of 20°C (low input). Turn-on deadband: 4°C, turn-off deadband: 2°C. This comparator determines whether the tank has sufficient stored energy to meet the heating demand.
- Comparator 3 compares the room setpoint temperature of 20°C (high input) with the actual room zone temperature (low input). Turn-on deadband: 1°C, turn-off deadband: -1°C. This comparator determines whether the room requires heating.
The 6 operating modes define the system behavior based on the combination of comparator states, and the 3 control outputs drive the collector pump (Output 1), the load pump (Output 2), and the auxiliary pump (Output 3) respectively. The controller uses a staggered output scheme where: when only solar collection is favorable, only the collector pump runs; when both solar collection and tank discharge are favorable, both the collector pump and load pump run; when the room needs heating but the tank is insufficient, the auxiliary pump is activated; and various combinations thereof.

Room setpoint temperature: Defined as a constant 20°C via an equation block.

Auxiliary heat source temperature: Defined as a constant 60°C via an equation block, representing an ideal boiler or district heating supply.

Psychrometric property calculators: Three psychrometric calculators determine the moist air properties (dry bulb temperature, humidity ratio, and atmospheric pressure as inputs) at different points in the air distribution loop. They operate in mode 4 (dry bulb temperature and humidity ratio known) and provide the processed air state to downstream components. The first calculator processes the building zone return air, the second processes the air after the auxiliary heat exchanger, and the third processes the air after the solar heat exchanger.

Output requirements:
1. Temperature curves: collector outlet temperature, tank bottom node temperature (node 5), tank top node temperature (node 1), room zone temperature, room setpoint temperature (20°C), and ambient dry bulb temperature. Temperature Y-axis range: -30 to 80°C.
2. Control signal curves: the 3 controller outputs (collector pump control, load pump control, auxiliary pump control), displayed as staggered signals with offsets of +15, +17, and +19 respectively for visual clarity. Control signal Y-axis range: 0 to 20.
3. The number of plots per simulation is calculated as (STOP - START) / 168, producing approximately one plot per week (about 21.6 plots total).
